Spec review companion · #117 · snapshot 275a774 · 2026-10-27

Go past a reclaim lock whose owner is dead

Read the open sections in about ten minutes. Everything closed is a look-up. A file:line chip jumps to the source line at the bottom, for when a claim needs checking.

Bug #117

The change

A process killed while it held the reclaim lock left state.json.lock.reclaim behind. From then on, every state update beside a dead main lock failed until someone deleted the file by hand. assessment:25

The fix goes past a dead reclaim lock along a chain of levels and never removes one, so only one process reclaims at a time. fix:10

8files changed fix:18
11reclaim tests, 1 changed fix:19
5checks passed test:19
4deviations fix:66

Root cause

The reclaim lock got the same owner record as the main lock, but its dead-owner case was left as an error for the user. assessment:45

Remediation

The next level is named by the dead owner's token. Every reclaimer walks the same chain, and the winner reads its passed levels again before it frees the main lock. assessment:52

This differs from the issue's literal "remove and retry": removing the dead file breaks the lock's mutual exclusion, so the reclaim goes past it instead. assessment:77

What moved since you last read it

Review round 3 made the timeout message read a level twice. assessment.md did not change.

ThenNowSource
A level released and taken again during the read got the delete adviceThe level is read twice, so its new live owner is namedfix:79

Three dated deviationsFourfix:79

The previous page listed 4 checks. None is resolved by this round.

How it works

Examples

These are the cases the tests run, as recorded in the bug notes. Nothing was run to build this page.

Dead main lock and dead reclaim lock

Expected: the update is written and the dead first level stays. This is the reported failure. test:19

A stale read of a level

A level's live owner released it after it was read. Expected: the reclaimer backs off and removes nothing. Fails with the re-read taken out. test:21

Removing passed levels (rejected)

A stalled reclaimer could win an old level while a new one held the first. That is why dead levels stay. assessment:93

Remove and retry (rejected)

Two reclaimers could both pass the token check, and one could remove a lock a live process took. assessment:86

What to check before approving

  1. The departure from the issue's wording. The dead file is passed, not removed. Check that this is the expected behaviour you want. assessment:77
  2. Dead files stay in the state folder. One per process killed while it held a level. assessment:151
  3. Pid reuse. A dead level whose pid goes to a new process blocks until that process ends, as the main lock does today. test:36
  4. No real killed companion in the tests. The tests write the files a killed process leaves. test:38

The assessment has no open questions. assessment:161

Look-ups

Glossary
  • Main lock: state.json.lock, held for each change of the state.
  • Reclaim level: a lock file that the process freeing a dead main lock holds, so only one process frees it.
  • Mutual exclusion: only one process changes state.json at a time.

# Bug Assessment: A reclaim lock whose owner is dead is never freed - **Slug**: 117-free-dead-reclaim-lock- **Created**: 2026-10-27- **Source**: pasted text (GitHub issue #117)- **Verdict**: valid- **Severity**: high ## Report (verbatim or summarized) Summarized from #117. `reclaimDeadLock` (`plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs`) frees a dead mainlock through a second lock, `state.json.lock.reclaim`. When that reclaim file belongs to a deadprocess, the code throws "The state lock ... .reclaim belongs to process N, which is no longerrunning. Delete ... and retry". Nothing in the code ever frees it. The reclaim file is held only for amoment, but a cancel's `taskkill /F` or Claude's hook kill can land there. From then on, every timethe main lock's owner is dead, every `updateState` throws: SessionEnd exits 1 and stops nothing,cancel fails, the worker's final write fails, until the user deletes the file by hand. Found by codereview on 2026-10-21, from the code. Expected: a reclaim lock whose owner is dead is freed the same way as a dead main lock. The error fora reclaim file that cannot be read stays. ## Symptom With a dead main lock and a dead reclaim lock beside it, every state update fails with "... .reclaimbelongs to process N, which is no longer running. Delete ... and retry". Expected: the dead reclaimlock is freed, then the dead main lock, and the update succeeds. ## Reproduction 1. Write `state.json.lock` with `{ pid: <dead pid>, token }` and `state.json.lock.reclaim` with   `{ pid: <dead pid>, token }` in a workspace's state folder.2. Call `updateState(workspace, ...)`.3. It throws the error above; the test "a reclaim lock whose owner is dead gives a clear error that   names it" (`tests/state.test.mjs:659`) pins this on `main`. ## Suspected Code Paths - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs` `reclaimDeadLock`, the `!linked` branch — throws when the reclaim file's owner is dead, instead of freeing it.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs` `describeLockBlocker` — the timeout message for a dead main lock beside a reclaim file that names no live process; it stays for the unreadable case.- `tests/state.test.mjs:659` — pins the throw. ## Root Cause Hypothesis The reclaim lock was given the same `{pid, token}` owner as the main lock, but its dead-owner case wasleft as an error for the user to fix by hand. A process killed while it holds the reclaim lock (onlyfor a moment, but kills do land there) leaves a file that no process ever frees. Confidence: high(the code and its test say so). ## Proposed Remediation **Preferred** (2026-10-27, after the plan review): free a dead reclaim lock by going past it, never byremoving a file that a live process may hold. The reclaim locks form a chain: the first is`state.json.lock.reclaim`, as today; when a level's owner is readable and dead, the next level is`state.json.lock.reclaim.<that owner's token>`. Every reclaimer of the same dead main lock walks thesame chain, so the first free level is the one they all contend on, and only one can link it. Thewinner first reads every level it passed once more: each must still hold the token it read. If onedoes not, or is gone or unreadable (its owner was alive when it was read, then released it and exited, so the liveness checkcame too late, and another process may now hold that level), the winner releases its own level andreturns, so `acquireStateLock` loops (plan review round 4). A dead owner never removes its level, soa passed level that still holds its token stays until the walk ends, and no other process can be onan earlier level. Then the winner does what the reclaim lock does today (re-check the main lock,remove it if its owner is still dead) and releases its own level, token-checked, as today. A deadlevel is never removed: itstays as a signpost to the next level, so the chain never changes under a reclaimer that stallsafter it read a level, and the first free level stays the same for every reclaimer (plan reviewround 2: removing passed levels let a stalled reclaimer win an old level while a new one held thefirst level). A level whose owner is alive, or that cannot be read, ends the walk as today: return,and `acquireStateLock` loops. A token that is not a plain UUID is treated as unreadable (it becomespart of a file name), and a token seen twice in one walk (a loop, only possible by tampering) endsthe walk as unreadable too. Dead levels add up only when a process is killed in the moment it holdsa level, so the walk has no fixed bound. The one temporary owner file serves every level and isremoved when the walk ends, also on an error. `describeLockBlocker` walks the same chain, so atimeout names the level that blocks (an unreadable one keeps today's message and advice). For theerror-path test, the link goes through an injectable `linkImpl` option, as `isPidAliveImpl` is. This differs from the issue's literal wording ("freed the same way as a dead main lock", "remove thereclaim file and try once more"): the dead reclaim file is not removed, the reclaim goes past it.It meets the issue's expected behaviour ("no state update fails because of a lock that no liveprocess holds"), and the literal way breaks the lock's mutual exclusion (Alternatives). The issuegets a dated scope line, and the PR says so. A walk that ends at a free level that it then loses(another process took it) times out with today's fallback message for a held lock, as today when noreclaim file exists. **Alternatives**:- Remove the dead reclaim file after a token re-check, then retry the link (the issue's wording):  the check and the removal are two steps, so two reclaimers can both pass the check, and the second  can remove the live reclaim file of the first. Both then reclaim the main lock, and one can remove a  main lock that a live process took since: two writes to `state.json` at once. Rejected in the plan  review (Codex), because the lock exists to prevent exactly that.- An atomic capture by rename and a give-back: narrows the window but still leaves the reclaim file  missing for a moment, so a third reclaimer can link it. Rejected.- The chain, with the winner removing the dead levels it passed (plan review round 1): a reclaimer  that stalls after it read a level can later win an old level while a new reclaimer holds the  first one, and both can reclaim at once. Rejected in plan review round 2 (Codex, Copilot). **Files likely to change**:- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs`- `tests/state.test.mjs`- `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` and the version files (patch release 1.0.20)- `docs/operations.md`: one sentence that names the reclaim files a killed process leaves, and that  they are not a stuck lock (it gives no advice to delete a lock file today). The spec folder  `specs/005-copilot-plugin-port/` mentions the old error, but a merged spec folder is history  (constitution, Implementation-to-Spec Consistency). **Tests to add or update**:- `tests/state.test.mjs:659`: a dead main lock beside a dead reclaim lock: `updateState` succeeds,  the update is written, the main lock and every temporary owner file are gone, the reclaimer's own  level is released, and the dead first level is still there.- Three dead levels: the walk goes past all of them and succeeds; a second dead main lock later  walks the same chain and succeeds again (the chain does not change).- A stalled reclaimer, through `isPidAliveImpl` as the test "a reclaimer that saw a dead owner does  not remove the lock that a live process took since" does: while the walker checks the dead first  level, the test frees the dead main lock and writes a live holder's main lock (another reclaim  done); the walker then links the second level, finds the main lock live at its re-check, removes  nothing, and releases its level; the live holder's main lock and the dead first level remain. A  variant: the second level is held by a live reclaimer, so the walker waits and leaves it.- A stale read: through `isPidAliveImpl`, the first level's owner is reported dead, but while it is  checked the test removes that level and writes it again with a live reclaimer's token (the old  owner released it, a new one took it). The walker links the next level, finds the first level  changed, releases its own level, removes nothing, and the update times out; the live reclaimer's  first level and the dead main lock are left as they were.- A live owner on a later level after a dead first level: the timeout message names that later level  (not `.reclaim`), and no reclaim file is removed.- Tokens in these tests are real UUIDs (a non-UUID token is now treated as unreadable); the  unreadable-reclaim test keeps its damaged content.- The link-order test at `tests/state.test.mjs:565-583` has no reclaim file and passes unchanged;  the new dead-first-level test checks its own order (`lock`, `reclaim`, `reclaim.<token>`, `lock`)  and that the temporary owner file is gone after it.- A passed level that is gone when the winner reads it again: the winner backs off as for a changed  token.- A dead first level followed by an unreadable second level: the walk ends, and the timeout message  names the second level with today's unreadable-file advice.- A loop of tokens (a level that names the first level's token again): the walk stops; the update  times out with the message that names that level.- A live owner on the next level (another reclaimer holds it): the update waits; that level's file  and the dead first level are left as they are.- A live owner on the first level beside a dead main lock: waits as today, with today's timeout  message (`describeLockBlocker` names `.reclaim`).- A level whose token is not a UUID: treated as unreadable, today's message names it.- An unexpected error on the link of a later level (`linkImpl` throws `EACCES` for it, the folder and  the files stay): the error comes out of `updateState`, and no temporary owner file is left.- The existing test "a reclaimer that saw a dead owner does not remove the lock that a live process  took since" passes unchanged.- The unreadable-reclaim test stays as it is. ## Risks & Considerations - Mutual exclusion holds: no reclaim level is removed except by its own owner, the dead levels never  change, so every reclaimer, also a stalled one, contends on the same first free level.- Dead levels stay in the state folder as small files (`state.json.lock.reclaim`,  `state.json.lock.reclaim.<uuid>`), one per process killed while it held a level; each walk reads  past them. `docs/operations.md` names them, so a reader knows they are not a stuck lock.- No change for a live reclaimer on the first level or an unreadable reclaim file.- A dead level whose pid the OS gives to a new process looks live and blocks the chain until that  process ends, the same limit the main lock has today (`isPidAlive`).- `isPidAlive` is the same check that frees a dead main lock today. ## Open Questions None. ## Constitution Check - **I. Upstream parity**: not relevant. The state lock's reclaim path is this repo's own (upstream  has no reclaim lock); no upstream name or behaviour changes.- **II. Only reviewed code**: met. Code written here; no new dependency.- **III. Copilot CLI through documented interfaces only**: not relevant. No Copilot call changes.- **IV. Safe by default**: met. A reclaim level is removed only by its own owner (token-checked, as  today); a dead level is never removed, so only one process reclaims at a time and only one process  writes `state.json` at a time.- **V. Cross-platform**: met. Same file operations as the main-lock reclaim, on every OS; the tests  run on ubuntu, macOS and Windows in CI.- **VI. Tested, including failure paths**: met. Tests for a dead reclaim lock, several dead levels, a  stalled reclaimer, a stale read of a level, a live next level, a live first level, the timeout  message for a later blocking level, a bad token, a token loop, an unexpected link error, and the  unreadable reclaim file. `docs/operations.md` names the reclaim files a killed process leaves. Patch release with its `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and the release  run after the merge.

# Bug Fix: A reclaim lock whose owner is dead is never freed - **Slug**: 117-free-dead-reclaim-lock- **Fixed**: 2026-10-27- **Assessment**: ./assessment.md- **Status**: applied ## Summary `reclaimDeadLock` no longer throws on a reclaim lock whose owner is dead. It goes past it along achain of reclaim levels, each named by the token of the dead owner of the level before, and neverremoves a dead level, so only one process reclaims the main lock at a time. ## Changes | File | Change | Notes ||------|--------|-------|| `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs` | modified | `nextReclaimLevel` gives the next level after a dead one (stops at an unreadable, live, non-UUID or repeated token); `reclaimDeadLock` walks the chain, reads every passed level again after it links one and backs off if one changed, then re-checks and frees the main lock as before; `describeLockBlocker` names the live process that frees the lock, or the unreadable level that blocks || `tests/state.test.mjs` | modified tests | the dead-reclaimer test now expects the recovery; tests for a chain of dead levels, live first and later levels, a non-UUID token, a token loop, an unreadable later level, a reclaimer that read the first level before another reclaim finished, stale reads (a level taken or released), and an unexpected link error || `docs/operations.md` | modified | names the reclaim files that a killed process can leave, and that they are not a stuck lock || `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` | modified | `### 1.0.20` entry || `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `plugins/copilot/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | modified | version 1.0.20 (`npm run bump-version`) | ## Diff Highlights (optional) ```jswhile (!tryLinkLock(ownerFile, reclaimFile)) {  const other = readLockOwner(reclaimFile);  const next = nextReclaimLevel(lockFile, other, seen, isAlive);  if (!next) {    return;  }  passed.push([reclaimFile, other.token]);  reclaimFile = next;}// ...if (passed.some(([file, token]) => readLockOwner(file)?.token !== token)) {  return;}``` ## Tests Added or Updated - `tests/state.test.mjs` "a reclaim lock whose owner is dead is passed by the next level, and the update is written" — the bug; the link order is `lock`, `reclaim`, `reclaim.<token>`, `lock`, and the dead first level stays.- "a chain of dead reclaim levels is walked to its end, and again for a later dead lock".- "a live owner on a later reclaim level makes the update wait, and the timeout names its owner".- "a live owner on the first reclaim level makes the update wait, and the timeout names its owner".- "a dead reclaim level with a token that is not a UUID stops the walk" and "... with a token loop ...".- "an unreadable reclaim level after a dead one stops the walk, and the timeout names it".- "a reclaimer that read the first level before another reclaim finished removes no live lock".- "a reclaimer whose read of a passed level is stale backs off when the level was taken by a live reclaimer" and "... was released" — both fail with the re-read taken out.- "a timeout while the reclaim chain is free says that the holder has ended".- "a reclaim level released while the timeout message reads it counts as free".- "a reclaim level released and taken again while the timeout message reads it names its new owner".- "a timeout after a dead reclaim level and a free next level says that the holder has ended".- "an unexpected error on the link of a later reclaim level comes out, and no temp file stays".- Unchanged and passing: the unreadable-reclaim test, "a reclaimer that saw a dead owner does not remove the lock that a live process took since", and the link-order test with no reclaim file. ## Local Verification - Commands run: `npm ci --include=dev`, `npm run build` → pass; `npm test` → 434 tests, 410 pass, 24 skipped, 0 fail (after review round 3: 437 tests, 413 pass); `npm run check-version` → 1.0.20; `claude plugin validate .` → pass.- With the re-read of passed levels taken out for one run, both stale-read tests fail. ## Deviations from Assessment - 2026-10-27: no `linkImpl` option. The unexpected-link-error test mocks `fs.linkSync` with  `t.mock.method`, as the existing link-order test does, so the plugin needs no new option.- 2026-10-27, review round 1 (`code-review`): a timeout while the holder is dead and the chain ends at  a free level now says "Process N has ended, and another process is freeing its lock; retry."  (the assessment kept today's "Process N holds the lock" there, which is wrong for a dead holder).  `describeLockBlocker` treats a level that was released during its walk as free, and  `nextReclaimLevel` runs the UUID and loop checks before the liveness check. Test added.- 2026-10-27, review round 2 (`code-review`): a level held by a live reclaimer now gives "Process N  is freeing the lock of ended process M; retry when it finishes." in place of the advice to delete  it (on `main` that advice also appeared for a live first level, and it could lead a user to delete  a lock that a running process held). A free chain gives "Process M has ended; retry." (no claim  that another process is at work). Tests updated, and one added for a level released while the  message reads it. The `CHANGELOG.md` entry names the new messages.- 2026-10-27, review round 3 (`code-review`): `describeLockBlocker` reads a level twice before it calls  it unreadable, so a level released and taken again during the read names its new live owner, not  the delete advice; it checks liveness once per level. Tests added for that case and for a walk past  a dead level to a free next level. ## Follow-ups - None. Upstream has no reclaim lock.
